classes.package_06_action: Walked all three source families covering every UK racecourse (The Jockey Club, 14 courses; Arena Racing Company, 16 courses; 30 independent operators) plus a national completeness cross-check against the British Horseracing Authority's own count of 59 Great Britain racecourses. All 60 Package 05 CAPACITY_STILL_UNVERIFIED_HIGH_VALUE_CANDIDATE racecourse rows assigned to researcher b were individually researched (official site fetched for 57 of 60; Wikipedia fallback used for the 3 not reachable - Redcar and Downpatrick due to fetch/TLS errors, plus Ffos Las due to a TLS error). Per-course capacity_context recorded honestly: most operators publish no capacity figure at all (confirmed absence, not a failed search); a handful publish attendance ranges (Salisbury 2,000-9,000; Fakenham up to 4,500+) or marketing/record attendance claims (Chester, Chelmsford City ~20,000+; Doncaster 60,000 St Leger 2026 record; Epsom 28,000 Derby Day 2026 record) which were used as MEDIUM-confidence evidence, explicitly labelled as attendance/record figures rather than stated formal capacities. CORRECTION APPLIED mid-task per coordinator review: Ffos Las was originally miscoded CONFIRMED_1000_PLUS on a circa-2009 PLANNED/proposed capacity figure alone; this has been corrected to CAPACITY_STILL_UNVERIFIED_HIGH_VALUE_CANDIDATE since a planned figure is not evidence of current capacity. Doncaster was upgraded from a Wikipedia-only figure (50,000) to the operator's own more recent 2026 record-attendance figure (60,000, OFFICIAL_OPERATOR). Follow-up operator-page fetches were also made for Epsom (corroborating record added), York and Hamilton Park (both checked, genuinely carry no usable current figure, Wikipedia sourcing retained) and Aintree/Cheltenham (both timed out twice, residual gap, Wikipedia sourcing retained).
source_families_checked: British Horseracing Authority / Great British Racing (completeness cross-check only)

Ffos Las's official ARC site also hit a TLS certificate error on repeated attempts; with only a planned/proposed 2009 figure available it is correctly CAPACITY_STILL_UNVERIFIED, not confirmed. Aintree and Cheltenham's own official Jockey Club pages timed out on a follow-up attempt to find an operator-sourced figure; both remain on Wikipedia-sourced MEDIUM-confidence capacities (75,000 and 67,500 respectively) as a result - a good next step for a future session. The Jockey Club's own Cheltenham press release about a 2023 Festival capacity change (68,500) was located via search but deliberately not cited as evidence since it was not directly fetched.

classes.package_06_action: Completeness check against EXTERNAL sport-specific sources (not a self-referential estate check). This is a residual bucket of 8 venues with no dedicated national 'stadium' directory of its own, so each of the 8 was individually identified and checked against the actual league/governing-body source that covers its sport: (1) Brick Community Stadium, Wigan = Wigan Athletic, confirmed via the EFL League One 2026-27 club list (Wikipedia) audited under FOOTBALL_GROUND. (2) Kingsholm Stadium, Gloucester = Gloucester Rugby, confirmed via the PREM Rugby 2026-27 club list (Wikipedia) audited under RUGBY_UNION_GROUND. (3) Sandy Park Stadium, Exeter = Exeter Chiefs, confirmed via the same PREM Rugby list. (4) Sixways Stadium, Worcester = Worcester Warriors, confirmed via the RFU Championship/Elior Champ Rugby 2026-27 club list (Wikipedia) audited under RUGBY_UNION_GROUND. (5) Swansea.com Stadium, Swansea = Swansea City, confirmed via the EFL Championship 2026-27 club list (Wikipedia). The remaining 3 were checked against external sources but NOT confirmed as covered by any sweep performed this session: (6) Post Office Road, Featherstone = Featherstone Rovers RLFC - checked against rugby league sources (search-identified: loverugbyleague.com, Wikipedia 2026 RFL Championship); Featherstone Rovers were REMOVED from RFL membership for the 2026 season (administration, December 2025) so the club is not currently a member of any professional rugby league division - no RFL Championship/League 1 completeness audit of the kind done for football/rugby union was performed this session, so this venue's currency is a genuine open question, not resolved here. (7) Queensway Stadium, Wrexham - confirmed (search-identified: welshathletics.org, Freedom Leisure) as a Wrexham Council-operated ATHLETICS stadium (Wrexham Athletics Club), unrelated to Wrexham AFC's football ground (STōK CaeRas, separately confirmed) - no national athletics governing-body completeness sweep was performed this session (only my 2 individually-assigned ATHLETICS_STADIUM rows were researched). (8) White Hart Lane Community Sports Centre, London (aka New River Stadium, Wood Green) - confirmed (Wikipedia) as home to London Skolars (rugby league) and Haringey Rhinos (rugby union) plus an athletics club; London Skolars play in RFL League 1, which was not audited this session.
